claims.text: Adding 1.5–3.0 at.% Si and using an 850 °C/950 °C stepped sintering profile will suppress Laves-phase formation in Mg-Nb-Ti-based alloys.
The Si addition and stepped profile will suppress Mg and other volatile-element loss.
The proposed processing will form a continuous nanoscale SiO2/Al2O3-like barrier network.
The processed Mg-transition-metal alloy will have a stabilized, single-phase-like BCC matrix.
The proposed stepped process will achieve greater than 95% relative density.
Si lowers the activation energy for solid-solution formation at 850 °C.
Si-containing alloys can form compact, self-healing silica layers that act as diffusion barriers against further oxidation.
A residual-oxygen-derived SiO2 layer will prevent Mg volatilization and internal oxidation in the proposed alloy.
An initial 850 °C hold permits densification without triggering B2+BCC or Laves-phase decomposition, while a final 950 °C hold completes densification.
Intermediate-temperature aging can enhance local chemical ordering and cause embrittlement in a multiphase HEA.
Standard isothermal sintering of Mg-transition-metal alloys at 900 °C produces a BCC plus Laves two-phase mixture.
Standard sintering at 900 °C causes significant Mg volatilization and porous microstructures.
The baseline 900 °C material has poor corrosion resistance.
The proposed material will exhibit a 50% reduction in oxidation weight gain relative to the baseline.
Suppressing brittle phase segregation will improve the alloy's ductility.
The proposed alloy will show a 20% increase in ductility.
Above 1000 °C, Mg volatility and SiO2 evaporation rates increase exponentially.
Si concentrations above 5 at.% may induce brittle Mg2Si formation.
Nanoscale Si-rich oxide precipitates inhibit grain-boundary diffusion of Mg and V.
Si may segregate to grain boundaries and a discontinuous oxide network may promote intergranular corrosion.

contradictions.description: The inert Ar atmosphere is specified to prevent premature oxidation, while the central mechanism requires residual oxygen to generate a continuous SiO2 network; no oxygen activity or dosing strategy is defined to reconcile these requirements.
